To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have created a Bose–Einstein condensed gas of rubidium atoms and that we have created quantized circulation (a quantized vortex) in that gas by using a laser beam to impart a well‐defined orbital angular momentum to the gas.
we have created a vortex lattice in a Bose–Einste in condensate and have measured the circulation of each lattice point.
we have created a Bose–Einstein (BE) condensate of 87Rb atoms with a large number of vortices and that these vortices are in a superfluid state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs).
the production of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in a ring-shaped trap and the creation of vortices within it.
the production, characterization, and manipulation of Bose-Einstein condensates of atoms in optical lattices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the experiment has demonstrated a Bose–Einstein condensed state in which the atoms have a quantized circulation.
the authors have demonstrated that a Bose–Einstein gas of atoms with spin‐3/2 can be prepared in a coherent state with quantized circulation.

the authors have demonstrated that Bose–Einstein condensed atoms in a magnetic trap can be made to flow without friction and with quantized vorticity, just like the known superconductors and superfluids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the quantum vortex in a dilute gas of bosons can be created by the application of a time-varying magnetic field.
the experiment is a demonstration of the existence of vortices in Bose condensates.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to make vortices in Bose–Einstein-condensed atoms, and we have measured the circulation and friction associated with those vortices.
